esm.readme:
## Auth

JWT access token (short-lived, returned in the response body) + refresh token (long-lived, httpOnly cookie).

- `POST /api/v1/auth/register` — create an account
- `POST /api/v1/auth/login` — get a new access token + refresh cookie
- `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` — exchange the refresh cookie for a new access token
- `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` — clears the refresh cookie
- `GET /api/v1/auth/me` — current user (requires `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`)

## Auth

`useAuth()` (from `src/auth/AuthContext.jsx`) talks to the exact JWT contract the backend composer's `auth-jwt*` modules expose: `POST /auth/{register,login,refresh,logout}`, `GET /auth/me`. The access token is kept in memory only; the refresh token is an httpOnly cookie the browser sends automatically (`credentials: "include"` in `src/auth/authApi.js`). `LoginForm` / `RegisterForm` / `AuthStatus` in `src/components/` are ready to drop into any page.

Set `VITE_API_URL` in `.env` to point at your backend (defaults to `http://localhost:4000/api/v1`, matching the backend composer's default).

nest-ts.readme:
## Database

MongoDB via `@nestjs/mongoose`. Set `MONGO_URI` in `.env` (defaults to a local instance on 27017). Registered in `AppModule` via `MongooseModule.forRootAsync(...)` (async so tests can override `MONGO_URI` before the connection is opened); feature modules register their own schemas with `MongooseModule.forFeature(...)`. Note: `mongodb-memory-server` is included so tests can run against a real in-memory MongoDB without a local install, whether or not you also picked the testing module.

## RBAC (Permission-based)

A role maps to a list of permissions in `config/permissions.js`, and routes declare which permission they need:

```js
router.get("/admin-check", requireAuth, requirePermission("admin:access"), handler);
```

Add a new role, or change what an existing role can do, by editing `config/permissions.js` only. See `routes/admin.routes.js` for a working example (`GET /api/v1/admin-check`).

## RBAC (Permission-based)

A role maps to a list of permissions in `src/config/permissions.ts`, and routes declare which permission they need:

```ts
@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard, PermissionsGuard)
@RequirePermissions("admin:access")
```

Add a new role, or change what an existing role can do, by editing `src/config/permissions.ts` only. See `src/admin/admin.controller.ts` for a working example (`GET /api/v1/admin-check`).

esm.readme:
## RBAC (Simple)

Each user has one `role`: `"user"` or `"admin"`. Protect a route with:

```js
router.get("/admin-check", requireAuth, requireRole("admin"), handler);
```

See `routes/admin.routes.js` for a working example (`GET /api/v1/admin-check`).

## Routing

[React Router](https://reactrouter.com) is wired up in `src/App.jsx`. Pages live in `src/pages/`; add a new `<Route>` there for each one.

`npm audit` will flag a moderate open-redirect advisory in this version (fixed only in v7, which currently has its own higher-severity advisory in the data-router/actions APIs this starter doesn't use) — it requires passing untrusted, attacker-controlled input into a `<Link>`/`useNavigate` target, which none of the code here does. Worth re-checking before you add anything that builds a redirect URL from user input.
